lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice using ska for near-future plans.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Colleagues talk during a Thursday break about plans for Friday evening or the weekend.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik discuss what they are going to do after work and during the weekend.

main_focus.name: ska for planned future
main_focus.description: Use ska plus infinitive to express intended or arranged future activities.
model_examples: Jag ska träffa en vän på fredag.
Ska du göra något i helgen?
main_focus.desired_presence: Use ska for plans naturally 5-7 times in the dialogue.

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use future-plan chunks that would fit real colleague small talk.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker asks about Friday or weekend plans.
dialogue_shape.middle: They exchange two or three planned activities with ska.
dialogue_shape.ending: They end with a friendly wish for the plan or weekend.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat ska plus infinitive enough to make the future meaning clear

sentence_focus: one question with Vad ska du göra
one sentence with ska laga mat or gå på bio
one sentence with a weekend time expression
one friendly closing about the plan
